## Natural history notes

A small tortricid moth characterized by yellowish to tan forewings with darker brown bands, mottling, and a folded resting posture typical of leafroller moths. In Florida, it is found in wooded and shrubby habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and other semi-open areas where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed concealed within folded or tied leaves, using silk shelters for protection and contributing to the broader food web as prey for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
